findings.claim: The 402 error message sent to clients states that recipient and counterparty analysis both require a paid Space, but only recipient analysis is actually gated on Core; counterparty analysis remains free, which the message misrepresents.
A doc comment repeats the same 'recipient/counterparty' inaccuracy, describing counterparty analysis as gated when it is not.

A comment states that the class lives in a 'routes/' folder, but the file is actually located at the module root, not under routes/.
A comment repeats the incorrect claim that this is part of safe-shield's 'routes/' layer, which does not match the actual file location.

SafeShieldService is still exported from the module even though nothing outside the module uses it anymore, since consumers now go through the ISafeShieldAnalysis token; this contradicts the module's own comment stating the service is never imported directly, and only the token should be exported.

CopilotCoreGatingGuard and CopilotCoreDisabledExceptionFilter are registered as module providers, but they don't need to be since @UseGuards and @UseFilters instantiate them directly; this is also inconsistent with QuotaExceededExceptionFilter, which is not registered as a provider.
A test casts a plain object with `{ id: userId } as Member` instead of using the existing memberBuilder() helper.
A test casts a partial analysis response using `as Awaited<...>` instead of using the recipient/counterparty response builders available in analysis-responses.builder.ts.

The same four negative test cases (unauthenticated, non-member, 402, unregistered Safe) are duplicated across both routes at the integration level and again at the unit level, when only one representative negative case per route should be tested in integration with the branch variations covered in unit tests.
